particulars: All names, dates, places, store names, dollar amounts, heights, weights, print point counts, sentence length and statute names are dropped.

items.record: The case began with two armed robberies of small stores, with no confession, plea or family death: 'a man with a gun robbed a Family Dollar store'.
items.reading: Guesses a domestic or child-death case built on a medical-legal diagnosis, or a plea-agreement statement of facts signed by the defendant.
items.loss: The kind of offense and the kind of case are misidentified.

items.record: The conviction rested on a fingerprint examiner's palm-print match plus cross-racial eyewitness picks made on a second viewing: 'made no identification on her first look... asked to see the photos again and selected Brown'.
items.reading: Lists possible methods (coerced confession, informant, bad forensics, drafted plea) without settling on one, and leans toward a confession or plea.
items.loss: The actual evidence that produced the wrongful account is missing.

items.record: Brown went to trial and never adopted the state's version. He denied it throughout: 'It wasn't me, your honor.'
items.reading: Suggests the defendant formally adopted the state's version and may feel 'the particular injury of having signed it'.
items.loss: The defendant's stance toward the official account is misdescribed.

items.record: The examiner's report falsely said he had searched the statewide database. The prints were 'loaded but never searched, although his report said they had been.'
items.loss: The specific false statement inside the forensic record that hid an alternative suspect is missing.

items.record: Running the prints years later matched another man: 'one of the three prints came from a man identified as Daris J.... who was taller and heavier than Brown'.
items.reading: Speaks generally of shifting ground (new science, recanting witness, a detective's pattern).
items.loss: The mechanism that overturned the account, a database hit on a third party, is missing.

items.record: Brown's physical build did not match the descriptions: medical records showed '5 feet 9 inches and 150 pounds' against a robber of 200–220 pounds, and his lawyer failed to show this.
items.loss: The mismatch between the accused and the described offender, and defence counsel's failure to use it, are missing.

items.record: The jury split: it acquitted on one robbery and convicted on the other only after an Allen charge, and a Black witness testified he was not the robber.
items.reading: Says the account felt true to jurors and was believed because it was clear and procedurally correct.
items.loss: The record shows doubt at trial, not smooth belief, and the reading misses this.

items.record: Evans testified that 'an officer pointed to Brown's photo and asked whether she was sure it wasn't him'.
items.loss: The suggestive police pressure on an identification witness is missing.

items.record: The trial exhibits were destroyed, and the court rejected the claim because there was 'no proof the clerk had acted in bad faith.'
items.reading: Gives generic rationalizing arguments: not newly discovered, harmless error, voluntary plea.
items.loss: The concrete episode of evidence destruction, and the bad-faith standard used to excuse it, are missing.

items.record: Police said they had no records of the searches and ignored the database question. The defence had to confirm with another agency and get a court order. A review found the examiner wrongly called prints valueless.
items.loss: The step-by-step fight for disclosure and the exposure of the examiner's pattern of error are missing.

items.record: Brown was released in 2021 while motions were pending, years before the conviction fell.
items.loss: The order of events, with release from prison coming well before vindication, is missing.

items.record: The state consented to a new trial and then dismissed the charge, 'while maintaining that Brown's trial lawyer had been effective.'
items.reading: Says the outcome is undecided at a threshold and predicts at best a partial correction such as an Alford plea or time-served re-plea.
items.loss: The actual resolution is missing: a consented new trial and dismissal, with the state conceding on evidence but not on counsel.

items.record: The family's role is limited to Brown having 'custody of my son' and being seen in the store 'often with a little boy'.
items.reading: Says the family is inside the harm, as in a child-death case, split between grief and suspicion.
items.loss: The family's position is misdescribed: in the record it serves as a character and alibi detail, not as the site of the alleged crime.

items.record: Brown denied it on the grounds that he 'worked full-time at a local factory, owned a $40,000 car', and payroll showed him clocking out at 5 p.m. on the second robbery date.
items.loss: The defendant's stable social position and the timing evidence offered against the accusation are missing.
